correctness.rationale: The published Ncib text, not the differently numbered arXiv v1, supplies the cited Definition 1.3(3), (1.9) and Example 1.1. On the even space both twists equal D=diag(gamma,1), while the odd line is central. Their invertibility and multiplicativity follow from the basis formulas, and the BiHom Jacobi sum on even arguments is D² times ordinary Jacobi; any odd input gives zero. For an even R the twist commutators have off-diagonal entries (1−gamma)c and (gamma−1)b. The product defect on (e1,e2) is −(a²+bc)e1−b(a+d)e2; odd inputs vanish and the two even inputs suffice by alternation. This is also the adjoint O-operator equation here: the even twists agree, and terms with odd inputs vanish. If gamma=1, b=0 forces a=0 and b≠0 forces d=−a,c=−a²/b. If gamma≠1, b=c=a=0. Consequently the printed R1 needs (gamma−1)a1=0 and R2 needs gamma=1, since its denominator b2 is nonzero. Over odd F_q the disjoint branches count q³ and q²(q−1) for gamma=1, and q² otherwise; with q−1 choices of lambda and q−2 other gammas the total is 3q²(q−1)². Reviewed the verification notes, artifacts/verify.py and its recorded verify_output.txt; the derivation proves the arbitrary-field result independently. This decision is for the stated adjoint O-operator interpretation, not a convention retaining only the product equation. The citation should distinguish the journal example and numbering from the preprint.
